blocks.text: The vision’s proclamation of YHWH’s holiness and Isaiah’s response in the temple belong to a wider emphasis in Isaiah: YHWH’s holiness is joined to justice and righteousness, and worship is rejected when it coexists with bloodshed, exploitation, or refusal to repair communal wrong.

Isaiah uses several kinds of speech and narration, including first-person reports, divine speech, royal narratives, communal voices, and personified figures. Speaker identity therefore needs to be established passage by passage. In this chapter, the first-person account of the vision gives way to the Lord’s speech and then to Isaiah’s commissioned message.

The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah. It broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition while also containing many spelling and substantive differences; other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings show that the book was actively transmitted and interpreted.
